metadata.title: Kling 2.5 — AI Video Built for High-Action Scenes | Oddbeam
metadata.description: Kling 2.5 Turbo on Oddbeam handles the shots other models fumble: running, choreography, combat at 1080p with believable physics, plus start/end frame control to lock a shot's entry and exit. 5 or 10 seconds, 100 credits — free on Unlimited.

hero.title: Kling 2.5 Video Generator
hero.description: Some shots need physics. Kling 2.5 Turbo is Kuaishou's motion specialist: reinforcement-learning-trained dynamics make running, group choreography, skating, and combat read as real weight and momentum at 1080p — and start/end frame control locks exactly where a shot enters and where it lands. 100 credits for 5 or 10 seconds.

usage.title: Direct the Motion, Not Just the Moment
usage.description: Kling 2.5 rewards prompts written like action notes — here is the workflow:

items.title: Describe Motion as a Sequence
items.description: Write what happens across the clip, not one frozen state — a character enters, crosses the room, stops at the window. Kling 2.5's prompt adherence follows temporal progression instead of freezing mid-action.

items.title: Animate a Still
items.description: Upload an image for image-to-video in 16:9, 9:16, or 1:1 — the model reads its style, lighting, and texture and keeps every frame consistent with the source while it moves.

items.title: Pin Start and End Frames
items.description: Give it the opening composition and the destination, and Kling 2.5 generates the transition between them — product in hand to product on surface, neutral face to reaction, wide shot to detail.

items.title: Pick 5s or 10s, Ship at 1080p
items.description: Choose the duration that fits the beat, generate at up to 1080p, and add sound in post — the clips are edited to be scored, so no audio pass blocks the render.

features.title: Why Action Shots Go to Kling 2.5
features.description: The capabilities that make it the motion specialist on Oddbeam:

items.title: Physics that holds at speed
items.description: Trained with reinforcement learning for real-world dynamics — gravity, inertia, fluid, hair, and cloth behave — which is why fast, dynamic movement reads as believable instead of floaty. It is the model to reach for when something in the frame is moving fast.

items.title: Start & end frame control
items.description: Lock the first frame and the last frame, and the model renders the journey between them — narrative control that makes reveals, transitions, and chainable shots land exactly where the edit needs them.

items.title: Temporal prompt adherence
items.description: Complex multi-step instructions — interactions, scene transitions, progression across a clip — are parsed deeply instead of collapsing to a single action, a noted upgrade over earlier Kling versions.

items.title: Style locked to the reference
items.description: High-intensity image conditioning keeps the color, lighting, texture, and atmosphere of your source image stable across every frame, even while the motion gets large.

items.title: 1080p at a working-model price
items.description: 100 credits per clip — 25 clips a month on Starter's 2,500 credits — with free generation on Unlimited. Broadcast-grade motion without flagship pricing.

testimonials.title: Built for Shots That Move
testimonials.description: How motion-heavy teams put Kling 2.5 to work.

items.name: Fight Choreographer
items.quote: Combat is where most models fall apart — limbs phase, weight vanishes. Kling 2.5 keeps the hits grounded, and start/end frames let me cut the fight into shottable beats.

items.name: Sports Content Producer
items.quote: Skating and dance clips at 1080p for 100 credits — the physics sell the move, and we score everything in post anyway, so the no-audio trade never touches us.

items.name: Commercial Director
items.quote: The reveal shot is a start-frame problem: product hidden, product shown. Kling 2.5 nails both endpoints and gives me a usable transition in one pass.

items.question: How much does Kling 2.5 cost per video?
items.answer: Kling 2.5 costs 100 credits per generation on Oddbeam for Starter and Pro plans, and Unlimited plan subscribers generate it for free — yearly Unlimited drops the rate to 10 credits. The Starter plan's 2,500 monthly credits cover about 25 clips at $29.99 per month.

items.question: How long can a Kling 2.5 clip be?
items.answer: Each generation runs 5 or 10 seconds — you pick the duration per shot. Longer sequences are built by chaining shots with start/end frame control, where one clip's final frame becomes the next clip's opening composition.

items.question: What is Kling 2.5 best at compared with other models?
items.answer: High-action motion: running, group choreography, skating, combat, and fluid dynamics. Its reinforcement-learning-trained physics and 1080p output make fast movement believable, which is exactly where one-shot cinematic models tend to break down.

items.question: Does Kling 2.5 generate start and end frame transitions?
items.answer: Yes. Provide the opening frame, the closing frame, or both, and the model generates the transition between them while holding style and lighting — the standard technique for product reveals and chained narrative beats.

items.question: Does Kling 2.5 have native audio?
items.answer: No — Kling 2.5 generates picture only, by design. Professional workflows score and mix in post anyway; if you need dialogue and ambience generated with the picture, use Seedance 2.5 or Veo 3.1 on Oddbeam, both of which render native audio.

items.question: Kling 2.5 or Seedance 2.5 — which should I pick?
items.answer: Pick Kling 2.5 for motion and budget: 1080p action clips at 100 credits with start/end frame control. Pick Seedance 2.5 for 30-second takes, 50 multimodal references, and native audio at 160 credits. One owns the movement, the other owns the sound.
